note: Tested "treats an improper BGP Extended Message as a fatal error"; Gap "follow the error-handling procedures of [RFC4271]"; Producer internal/component/bgp/reactor/relay_recovery.go::admitRecovery. Independent rejudgment from complete RFC 8654 and RFC 4271 Sections 6 and 6.1, every tagged unit, and the current reader/publication and recovery boundaries. RFC 8654 Section 5 says, "Similarly, any speaker that treats an improper BGP Extended Message as a fatal error MUST follow the error-handling procedures of [RFC4271]." Extracting readFrame preserves exact Bad Message Length notification, Event21, transport closure and the pre-body limit check. Header helpers assert returned notification values or no error; they do not observe socket or route cleanup. Actual TCP tests first establish real received routes, Loc-RIB state and downstream advertisements, then assert exact 1/2 Data 1001, EOF, Idle, timer/context/session cleanup, source storage removal and both downstream withdrawals. The alternate-best carrier checks both replacement attributes together on recipient TCP through a causal post-recovery marker, a single Loc-RIB replacement and withdrawal without a survivor. The adjacent 4096-octet control retains the original session/resources/routes and forwards its changed MED without notification or withdrawal. These assertions remain useful after the shared-reader extraction. RFC 4271 Section 6 also requires withdrawal or replacement before final invalid-route deletion. None of these end-state observations measures the last invalid-route or advertisement owner's lifetime through outbound admission; the tests explicitly disclaim that proof. admitRecovery stages owned references and dispatches completion-bound work, but reading that implementation cannot substitute for a lifecycle observation or a discriminating fault at its final-owner boundary. The existing partial annotation remains accurate and earns zero whole-requirement credit. No new execution or imported ordering conformance is claimed.
